cells.tense: There's enough in what you've made to stop and stand in it, and that's what you're doing.
cells.ask: Follow what already moves you into one concrete act that needs no preparation.
cells.core:
This is a person who wants something specific and can feel the wanting pointing somewhere real. When it goes well here, the light you steer by is steady and you can enjoy the distance still to travel without needing it closed today. You wake knowing which direction you lean, and the leaning is pleasant instead of urgent.

That is where you are standing now. What you've imagined and what you're reaching for have stopped competing, so direction shows up as appetite rather than obligation. Let this steadiness feed one real step, taken because it draws you and not because you owe it.
cells.sheetLine: You're shaping what you love, and the joy is doing the steering.
cells.verb: feeling what was imagined until the abundance is real
cells.place: the pull toward the light you steer by

cells.tense: You're already living at the destination you haven't built yet, and the arrival keeps slipping further out.
cells.ask: Pick the vision you'd tend if no one would ever see it, and give it one honest hour a week.
cells.core:
When this goes well, the pull toward light works as a compass and not a deadline. You can hold a picture of what you want without needing it finished, and the wanting keeps you moving at a pace the thing itself can survive. There's a pleasure in the tending, not just in the having.

Right now the whole harvest has to be visible before you'll stop reaching, so the reaching has hardened into pushing. What was a pull turns into a grip on the outcome, and the abundance you wanted keeps moving further out. Tend one thing slowly instead, without checking whether it's grown fast enough, and let care replace hurry.
cells.sheetLine: You're reaching for the harvest and tugging the roots.
cells.verb: feeling what was imagined until the abundance is real
cells.place: the pull toward the light you steer by

cells.tense: You wanted something once, and you're still standing where you stopped wanting it.
cells.ask: Say one true thing about what you want, out loud, before you've decided how to feel about it.
cells.core:
At its best this seat is an open line to what you actually desire, so every week has a direction you didn't have to talk yourself into. You notice what draws you, you follow it, and the following is easy because it isn't argued.

That line has gone quiet. The pull is still in you somewhere — you can find it when you look — but you've stopped letting it point at anything, and days pass with no want driving one of them. Let yourself know one thing plainly, before you turn it into a plan or a feeling. Knowing comes before declaring, and the wanting can carry a next step.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped pointing at the light, not noticing it.
cells.verb: feeling what was imagined until the abundance is real
cells.place: the pull toward the light you steer by

cells.tense: The current is already moving through you and you tell the story as though it's just the weather.
cells.ask: Say out loud what you're actually reaching toward, once, plainly, as yours.
cells.core:
When this seat is clear-eyed, a person knows what they're steering by and can say it in a sentence. The dreaming comes after the living has been digested, so the vision is grounded in what actually happened rather than in what might. You move toward light you can name.

By now you're living inside something you built — the shape of the days, the direction they lean, the light you keep choosing — and you call it the ordinary facts of your life. The wanting is steering while you call it background, and you rarely hear yourself prefer anything. Name what you're reaching for as your own. A small honest choice, made simply enough to stay kind, is the practice, and the pull gets stronger the moment its author says so.
cells.sheetLine: The light you're steering by is yours and hasn't heard you say so.
cells.verb: feeling what was imagined until the abundance is real
cells.place: the pull toward the light you steer by
